note: See grant_contract.mjs. Entries may only be REMOVED, never edited to hide a regression. Migration 031 closed 43 of the 47 findings from this file's first run. Migration 032 closed the one rule-I finding that was a live boundary defect. **Migration 034 closed all five rule-C findings: R13-conn was decided on 8 September 2026 as Option 2, one LOGIN role per worker role, so every privilege-holding role is now reachable.** The three I entries that remain are one question, not three bugs: HP-ADR-004 §2 seeds exactly one region, so none of them can leak today; each becomes a real boundary the day a second region is added under Migration Pack §2.2, which is the moment they must be settled and the last cheap moment to do it.

entries.key: I-pseudonym-readable-unbounded|metrics_role|obs.response_audit|can SELECT; RLS is off, so every row is visible
entries.detail: can SELECT; RLS is off, so every row is visible
entries.why: obs.response_audit has no data_region column, so there is nothing for a policy to bound on. HP-ADR-004 §2 seeds exactly one region ('IN'; 'DE' is deliberately not seeded), so today this table cannot hold a row from a region metrics_role should not see — the boundary is the deployment, not the schema. That stops being true the day a second region is added, and adding the column later is more expensive than adding it now, which is why this is an item rather than a shrug.
entries.item: SEC-2 — the three pseudonym-bearing tables with no data_region column. Settle before the second region is admitted (HP-ADR-004 §3.3, Migration Pack §2.2). The response_audit_event half needs the audit-chain question answered first (HP-RB-001, C-30).

entries.key: I-pseudonym-readable-unbounded|hp_app|public.response_audit_event|can SELECT; RLS is off, so every row is visible
entries.detail: can SELECT; RLS is off, so every row is visible
entries.why: public.response_audit_event has no data_region column, for the same reason as obs.response_audit and one more: it is HP-RB-001's hash-chained immutable audit log, so adding a column changes what every row_hash covers. That is a migration with a chain rewrite in it, not a column addition, and it does not belong inside SEC-1. Immutability and the narrow grants (INSERT/SELECT only, no UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE, plus forbid_mutation()) are real controls and are unaffected — what is missing is a REGION boundary, not a write boundary.
entries.item: SEC-2 — the three pseudonym-bearing tables with no data_region column. Settle before the second region is admitted (HP-ADR-004 §3.3, Migration Pack §2.2). The response_audit_event half needs the audit-chain question answered first (HP-RB-001, C-30).

entries.why: NOT R13-conn — that decision is closed. This role is unreachable ON PURPOSE. Its one grant is INSERT on principal.patient_attribute_confirmation, and nothing in the codebase writes that table: the confirmation UI does not exist yet. Migration 034 §1 withholds LOGIN from roles with no caller, the same reasoning that had migration 031 revoke thirty speculative grants — each individually defensible, none with a caller. dqe_role and erasure_role are in the same position but hold no grants, so rule C does not reach them.
entries.item: Closes in the migration that builds the confirmation UI (CGP-001 §8.3, the reviewer console). Give it LOGIN there, not before.

entries.key: M-policy-with-no-grant|PUBLIC|principal.patient_attribute|RLS policy p_pa_own exists; no application role holds any privilege
entries.detail: RLS policy p_pa_own exists; no application role holds any privilege
entries.why: DELIBERATE, and the only entry of this rule that is. The request path must read patient attributes ONLY through principal.fetch_attribute_envelope, which writes principal.attribute_access_log on every read (§3.8.2) and raises HP-ESC 3.8.2 for inferred rows outside CONFIRMATION_UI. A direct SELECT grant would let the request path read health attributes with no record that it did — which is the guarantee the envelope exists to provide. p_pa_own is therefore the backstop for the day somebody adds that grant anyway, not dead code: migration 041 §3 asserts no such grant exists and fails if one appears.
entries.item: Permanent. Closes only if attribute access stops being envelope-mediated, which would be a §3.8.2 amendment.
